# Physiology, Blood Brain Barrier

**Authors:** Rohin Gawdi, Karlie R. Shumway, Prabhu D. Emmady

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

The blood-brain barrier (BBB), first described by Paul Ehlrich (1885), is a highly selective semi-permeable membrane between the blood and brain interstitium. This unique barrier allows cerebral blood vessels to regulate the movement of molecules and ions between the blood and the brain. The BBB is composed of cerebral capillary wall endothelial cells (ECs) held together via tight junctions (TJs). These TJs, surrounded by pericytes, astrocytes, and the basal lamina, contribute to the highly selective nature of the BBB, limiting the passage of substances from the blood to the brain more so than any other capillaries in the body. See Figure. Blood Brain Barrier.
